If it is considered necessary to plug a hole, materials will be on board to do this. It would consist of ordinary cement and bentonite.
In the Ross Sea, the currents flow clockwise. Oil slicks would circulate but be gradually dispersed into lower latitudes. At the same time there would be slow microbial degradation, probably with no accompanying oxygen deficits. These hydrocarbons will be ultimately dissipated. However, it is likely that penguins, other marine birds, and seals will be affected in a similar manner to surface dwelling pelagic organisms in lower latitudes. Should hydrocarbons also be released into the sea below the ice shelf, they would also have a local, possibly severe, temporary impact on any biota there. It is on the basis of (a) the remote possibility of an uncontrolled release of hydrocarbons, but (b) the potentially serious, albeit over a period of years insignificant, impact on the environment that we have assigned a value of 5 in Table 2.
19. Operational Failures. With respect to impact on the environment, operational failures can generally be managed without great environmental impact at the operation and camp sites. However, failure in the drilling operation could result in loss of the drill stem and casing (Hole No. 2) in or below the drill hole. These elements could not be recovered.
